arxiv:2610.35835.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
arxiv:2610.35835.abstract: Human oversight is a pillar of AI safety. It is often exercised by a human in the loop (HITL) who approves critical actions taken by an AI agent.

arxiv:2610.35725.abstract: The gap between AI capability deployment and safety assurance is structural and cannot be closed through internal evaluations alone. arxiv:2610.35716.title: Audit Where Hacks Pay: Budgeted Strong-Verifier Audits Against Reward Hacking in GRPO
arxiv:2610.35716.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards trains on cheap checks, such as unit tests, that a policy can learn to game, while a stronger check is too expensive to run on every rollout. We study how to spend a limited strong-verifier budget in GRPO, separating which weakly passing rollouts to audit from what reward…

arxiv:2610.35497.title: When Fine-Grained Credit Assignment Helps and Hurts: Multimodal Agentic Reinforcement Learning through Video Editing
arxiv:2610.35497.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for training multimodal agents to reason and use tools. However, it remains unclear when fine-grained credit assignment improves learning and when it fails to improve task performance.

arxiv:2610.34965.title: The Target Agent Is Its Own Best Critic but a Poor Proposer: Self-Improved Red Teaming
arxiv:2610.34965.abstract: Automatic red teaming increasingly relies on large language models (LLMs) to iteratively diagnose failed attacks and propose improved adversarial prompts or injections. Although prior work strengthens this loop through prompt engineering and search-harness design, the mechanisms underlying its two core roles…

arxiv:2610.34855.title: DecoyCount: Evaluating Visual-Reasoning Misalignment in Counting
arxiv:2610.34855.abstract: Visual counting benchmarks report whether vision-language models produce the correct number, but not whether errors arise from perception or reasoning. We introduce DecoyCount, a benchmark built from 1,660 real-world images with designed decoys across seven mechanisms, along with paired prompts: a neutral question, a…

arxiv:2610.34770.title: The Impact of Personalized AI Response Suggestions on Content Creators' Direct Messaging
arxiv:2610.34770.abstract: Direct messaging is often employed by social media content creators to directly interact with followers. Those creators attempt to engage with followers in private communication, but they often encounter a large volume of messages.

arxiv:2610.34756.title: Mechanistic Insights into LoRA: Layer Sparsity for Adaptive Fine-Tuning via Path Patching
arxiv:2610.34756.abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has emerged as the dominant paradigm for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models. Standard all-layer LoRA applies adaptation throughout the transformer, despite heterogeneous contributions from its components.

arxiv:2610.34711.title: Intervene, Calibrate, Discover: Learning Causal Structure from Pixels
arxiv:2610.34711.abstract: Learning high-level causal variables from low-level observations is a central problem for artificial intelligence. With known node semantics but an unknown graph, visual readout errors can misalign model settings with environment intervention values.

arxiv:2610.34705.title: Safe by Benchmark, Unsafe in Practice: Lessons from 1331 Child-Related AI Incidents
arxiv:2610.34705.abstract: AI systems are increasingly present in children's everyday environments: education, entertainment, social networks, and toys. Their safety is typically assessed at the model level, through benchmarks, red-teaming, and content filtering.

arxiv:2610.34535.title: SentryBench: A Cost-Sensitive Benchmark for Adversarial Robustness of Tool-Using LLM Agents in Public-Safety Deployments
arxiv:2610.34535.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly wired to consequential tools that send public alerts, dispatch responders, and query citizen records, where one erroneous tool call carries real-world cost. Existing agent-safety benchmarks measure generic harm or prompt-injection success and implicitly treat refusing…

arxiv:2610.34375.title: Whether or Where? Tail Calibration Signals Finite-Budget Reward Hacking in Best-of-N Selection
arxiv:2610.34375.abstract: Best-of-N (BoN) inference returns the candidate with the highest proxy reward, so a larger $N$ tests the proxy's extreme tail more than its average ranking quality. We show that the exact BoN value is a Beta-weighted integral of conditional true reward over within-prompt score quantiles.

arxiv:2610.34365.title: SEEK: Skill Extraction with Evolving Knowledge against Frontier Science Agents
arxiv:2610.34365.abstract: Science agents increasingly package domain expertise as reusable skills that plan analyses, select tools, and execute workflows. This modularity creates a confidentiality risk: the interactions that deliver a skill's capability can also reveal the skill itself.

arxiv:2610.34074.title: Identically Trained Language Models Break on Different Jailbreaks
arxiv:2610.34074.abstract: Jailbreak benchmarks test one checkpoint and treat which jailbreaks break it as a property of its pretraining data and safety training. We ask whether another pretraining run of the same data, given the same safety training, would break on the same jailbreaks.

arxiv:2610.33813.title: Task Format as a Factor in Adaptation: A Controlled Comparison of LoRA and Full Fine-Tuning for Prompt-Safety Classification
arxiv:2610.33813.abstract: Fine-tuning a language model for classification involves many design decisions. Comparisons of low-rank adaptation (LoRA) with full fine-tuning are common but often confounded, and task format is rarely studied.

arxiv:2610.33605.title: Data Governance for Generative and Agentic AI : Technology, Law, Economics, and Security
arxiv:2610.33605.abstract: This book develops a unified governance framework for systems that retrieve, generate, infer, remember and act on information from large language models and retrieval augmented pipelines to autonomous multi agent systems. Eleven chapters and eight appendices integrate three disciplinary lenses-technology, law and…

arxiv:2610.33512.title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
arxiv:2610.33512.abstract: Rubric-based rewards enable effective reinforcement learning on non-verifiable tasks. However, because these rewards are typically defined as a weighted measure of rubric coverage, models are trained primarily to maximize a recall objective.

arxiv:2610.33353.title: Detecting Temporal Concepts in Video Transformers via a No-False-Positives Test
arxiv:2610.33353.abstract: Video models have the architecture to support encoding temporal aspects of the input, i.e. concepts that require more than one frame to define, like object movement. However, because motion and appearance change are entangled, a feature that appears to encode temporal concepts like object movement may instead encode…

arxiv:2610.33240.title: NewsBench: Expert-Grounded Evaluation of Epistemic Quality in AI News Reporting
arxiv:2610.33240.abstract: As frontier AI systems increasingly serve as sources of political and current-events information, evaluating the epistemic quality of their responses is now especially consequential. Existing evaluations often focus narrowly on ideological alignment, rely on measures not validated for this setting, or depend on…

arxiv:2610.33233.title: Distilling Expert Judgment at Scale
arxiv:2610.33233.abstract: Frontier AI models are increasingly deployed on topics where the stakes are high and expert judgment is required, including healthcare, defense, finance, governance, and politics. We present a general methodology for distilling expert human judgment into automated evaluation systems that operate at scale.

arxiv:2610.33180.title: Propensities Please: Exposing Alignment-Faking LLMs using Synthetic Document Finetuning
arxiv:2610.33180.abstract: Alignment evaluations aim to assess whether large language models would engage in dangerous misaligned behaviour. Misaligned and evaluation-aware models might engage in alignment faking, where they pursue a hidden goal, but conceal this behaviour when they suspect effective oversight such as during training…

arxiv:2610.33072.title: VLMProbe: An Open-source Library for VLM Probing and Interpretation
arxiv:2610.33072.abstract: Understanding how vision-language models use visual information requires connecting internal representations to model behavior. We present vlmprobe, an open-source library that integrates lens readouts, attention attribution, causal interventions, and sparse autoencoder (SAE) analysis within a common model interface.

arxiv:2610.32780.title: AI Alignment for Digital Democracy: Fairer Voters Representation against LLM Biases
arxiv:2610.32780.abstract: AI representation is emerging in digital democracy, assisting in voter emulation and decision-making. arxiv:2610.32281.title: "Not" is Not Lost in Translation: A Causal Analysis of Negation Representations in Multilingual LLMs
arxiv:2610.32281.abstract: Negation occurs in every language, yet its surface realization differs drastically. Despite this, multilingual large language models (LLMs) translate negation robustly, raising the question of whether they share an underlying representation of negation across languages.

arxiv:2610.32255.title: Anti-coherence Regularized Absolute Scaling for Out-of-Distribution Detection
arxiv:2610.32255.abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is recognized as a critical problem in AI safety. SCALE is an effective post-hoc OOD detection method in the activation-shaping family that requires no training data and rescales penultimate activations using a percentile-based magnitude ratio.

arxiv:2610.32208.title: Do VLAs Know They Will Fail? Interpretable Success and Failure Patterns in Physical AI Systems
arxiv:2610.32208.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as powerful general-purpose robot policies, but their successes and failures remain difficult to diagnose and understand. In this work, we show that sparse autoencoder (SAE) representations of OpenVLA activations contain outcome-predictive information and can be used to…

arxiv:2610.32114.title: Tampered ML: Evaluating LLM Judgment of Machine Learning Research
arxiv:2610.32114.abstract: One approach to accelerating progress on AI alignment is to automate parts of alignment research itself. Doing so requires systems that can perform reliably on hard-to-supervise research tasks, including identifying flaws in research proposals and evaluating whether a proposed experiment supports its intended claim.

arxiv:2610.32059.title: Concept Acupuncturist: An Efficient and Precise Concept Erasure Method for Diffusion Models via Sparse Autoencoders
arxiv:2610.32059.abstract: Diffusion-based image generation models produce high-quality images but may generate harmful or policy-violating content, motivating machine unlearning (MU) to selectively remove target concepts while preserving general capabilities. However, existing MU approaches often struggle with the distributed and entangled…

arxiv:2610.32007.title: MI-MIDI 2: From Observation to Control with Sparse Autoencoders in Text-to-MIDI Generation
arxiv:2610.32007.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) can expose features of a generative model without predefined labels, but in language models the evidence used to interpret these features has proven an unreliable guide to which of them steer the output. Whether interpretations of SAE features predict control in music generators has not, to…

arxiv:2610.31972.title: Reproducible Evaluation as the Substrate for Safe Prompt Compression in Production Agents
arxiv:2610.31972.abstract: Evaluating conversational agents that act on live, mutable enterprise data is hard: replayed sessions drift as backend state changes, and a benchmark built today can silently go stale as the data it describes moves on. We present an offline evaluation harness for a production conversational agent that stays…

arxiv:2610.31937.title: $M^3$: A Multi-LLM System for Multi-Turn Jailbreaking as a Markov Decision Process
arxiv:2610.31937.abstract: Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to carefully orchestrated multi-turn interactions that progressively bypass safety mechanisms. However, many existing red-teaming approaches rely on heuristics or impose strong assumptions that limit their applicability in fully black box settings.

arxiv:2610.31894.title: TaxoSAE: Rethinking Sparse Autoencoders through Taxonomic Logic
arxiv:2610.31894.abstract: Recent Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) decompose the representations of large language models (LLMs) into interpretable features, enabling precise readout and control of encoded knowledge. However, existing SAEs treat each feature as a standalone unit, whereas real-world knowledge is often taxonomically organized.

arxiv:2610.31733.title: Learning to Be Monitored: Causal Bounds and Intervention-Aware Post-Training Recipes for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
arxiv:2610.31733.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring aims to detect potentially harmful behaviors in large language models (LLMs) from their CoTs. Intervention-based evaluations measure this property by asking whether a monitor can detect the role of an intervention from the CoT when the targeted behavior occurs, typically using…

arxiv:2610.31713.title: Omni-UBench: Benchmarking Omni-Modal LLM-based Guardrails Across Safety, Utility, and Reliability
arxiv:2610.31713.abstract: Advances in Omni-modal Large Language Models (OLLMs) have enabled increasingly seamless human-AI interaction, but their unified processing of heterogeneous modalities also expands the attack surface, allowing adversaries to exploit richer input compositions to circumvent safety alignment. To counter such risks…

arxiv:2610.31520.title: The Geometry of Metaphor: Probing and Steering Metaphor Representations in Large Language Models
arxiv:2610.31520.abstract: Metaphor is a crucial aspect of human cognition. As such, we would like to understand how it is represented in large language models (LLMs) and how it might be controlled.

arxiv:2610.31331.title: Harmful Responses Are Jailbreak Templates: Transferring Autoregressive Jailbreaks to Diffusion Language Models
arxiv:2610.31331.abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) enable flexible masked generation through bidirectional context modeling, but this capability also introduces a distinct jailbreak attack surface. We find that a harmful response to a given query naturally serves as an effective jailbreak template: simply masking a subset of its…

arxiv:2610.30934.title: Verbalizing Activation Differences with Natural Language Autoencoders
arxiv:2610.30934.abstract: Activation verbalizers translate the internal representations of large language models into human-readable text. The recently proposed natural language autoencoders (NLAs) learn this by reconstructing activations through a natural language bottleneck.

arxiv:2610.30822.title: TESSA: A Governance-Oriented Custom GPT for SME Guidance under the EU AI Act: Design, Implementation, and Evaluation
arxiv:2610.30822.abstract: The increasing adoption of generative AI presents new opportunities while raising AI governance and regulatory challenges, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) navigating the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act (EU AI Act). To support AI governance education, this study developed TESSA, a…

arxiv:2610.30803.title: What Lies Beyond Perception: A Partition Theory of the Limits of AI Evaluation and Oversight
arxiv:2610.30803.abstract: Replacing the judge can move a benchmark score, and models can be trained to hide capabilities. Both put the evaluator in question: what can it certify?

arxiv:2610.30727.title: Faithful Latent Harm Monitors Work No Better Than the Models Own Behaviour at a Matched False Alarm Rate
arxiv:2610.30727.abstract: Large language models have been reported to encode the harmfulness of a request separately from their decision to refuse it, and latent safety monitors such as Latent Guard build on this report by classifying prompts as harmful from the internal activations of the model, with the aim of catching harmful intent even…

arxiv:2610.30582.title: Model Organisms of Collusion: Corrective Transfer in Untrusted Monitors
arxiv:2610.30582.abstract: AI control protocols aim to get useful work from models that may be misaligned by monitoring their behaviour. One approach uses a second copy of the same model as the monitor.

arxiv:2610.30474.title: Rethinking SAE Evaluation: An Atomic Interpretable Unit Framework Reveals Hidden Polysemanticity and Redundancy
arxiv:2610.30474.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) were originally motivated by discovering monosemantic features, a property that characterizes individual features but does not specify what the learned feature set should look like as a whole. As SAEs have increasingly been adopted for attribution, circuit discovery, and intervention…

arxiv:2610.30182.title: Detecting AI Training in Datacentre Power
arxiv:2610.30182.abstract: AI governance agreements require methods to detect large model training runs on a monitored computing cluster, without trusting the operator. We develop a method to detect synchronous model training in facility-level power by Viterbi tracking of the wandering iteration cadence.

arxiv:2610.30051.title: From Reasoning to Action: Benchmarking Frontier AI Models on LIBERO-10 Robot Manipulation Tasks
arxiv:2610.30051.abstract: Recent advances in frontier AI models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual understanding, reasoning, planning, and tool use, raising the possibility of using general-purpose AI models for robot manipulation without task-specific training. arxiv:2610.30006.title: Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders
arxiv:2610.30006.abstract: AI-generated text detectors are increasingly deployed in consequential settings---peer review, education, admissions, journalism, and content moderation---where their outputs directly affect individuals. Yet the strongest detectors are fine-tuned neural classifiers whose decisions are opaque, while transparent…

arxiv:2610.29734.title: Monitorability Is Trainable: Post-Training for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
arxiv:2610.29734.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is one of the few practical tools available for overseeing capable AI systems, but it is fragile: a model's reasoning is only useful to a monitor if it remains coupled to what the model actually does. This coupling can be degraded during training through, for example, CoT compression…

arxiv:2610.29225.title: Beyond Binary Labels: Diagnostic Evaluation of LLM Safety with Prompt-Level Rubrics
arxiv:2610.29225.abstract: Current LLM safety benchmarks predominantly rely on binary safe or unsafe labels, lacking explanatory depth and suffering from low consistency across automated judges. To address this, we introduce DiagSafe, a diagnostic evaluation framework that moves beyond binary classification by employing prompt-level rubrics.

arxiv:2610.29129.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Realistic Scenarios Through Representation Engineering
arxiv:2610.29129.abstract: Reward hacking is a major problem in current production machine learning systems, resulting in costly and dangerous failures. Here we study how to monitor for and mitigate reward hacking in realistic settings, including tool calls and long contexts.

arxiv:2610.28992.title: Language Impairment as a Lens onto Large Language Models
arxiv:2610.28992.abstract: Although large language models (LLMs) encode language in highly distributed spaces, they remain vulnerable to focal disruptions---a phenomenon strikingly similar to how localized brain damage causes clinical aphasia in humans. To investigate this theoretical tension, we ask whether LLMs possess a functional structure…

arxiv:2610.28966.title: Black-Box Red-Teaming of Multi-Agent Systems via Reinforcement Learning
arxiv:2610.28966.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems (MAS) to accomplish complex tasks. Prior black-box red-teaming attacks mainly focus on single agents, but we find that these methods are far less effective in MAS, where multiple sub-agents may not directly interact with the user.

arxiv:2610.28904.title: Tropical Cyclone Attributes in Sparse Autoencoder Features of an AI Weather Model
arxiv:2610.28904.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) weather models now forecast weather events skillfully, but how they represent these events internally remains unknown. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) provide sparse features for probing hidden states, but how information about multiple physical attributes of an event is organized across them…

arxiv:2610.28819.title: LIFT: Scoped Constraints for Evaluating and Training Instruction Following
arxiv:2610.28819.abstract: Common instruction following (IF) benchmarks, such as IFEval, evaluate the ability of language models (LMs) to follow simple constraints that can easily be verified programmatically. These same constraints, in turn, are used as reward signals for reinforcement learning.

arxiv:2610.28810.title: Combining Long-Term Memory and LLMs Comes at a High Cost: From Prompt Injection to Persistent Compromise
arxiv:2610.28810.abstract: The widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence in recent years has brought a parallel rise in prompt injection and jailbreak attacks. By embedding malicious instructions, these exploits manipulate language models to bypass intended behavior and operational boundaries.

arxiv:2610.28799.title: Where Do Legal Factors Live in LLMs?
arxiv:2610.28799.abstract: In case-based legal reasoning, legal professionals identify legally significant fact patterns in a new dispute and compare them with those of decided cases. arxiv:2610.28707.title: SimHack: Predicting the onset of detectable reward hacking before RL training
arxiv:2610.28707.abstract: When training LLMs to code with reinforcement learning, reward hacking is often detectable but difficult to prevent, since (a) environment hardening is increasingly difficult as training environments grow more complex; and (b) training-time interventions incentivize models to obfuscate hacking behavior to bypass…

arxiv:2610.28607.title: Benchmarking Arabic Dialects for Math Problems
arxiv:2610.28607.abstract: Mathematical reasoning remains underexplored for low-resource languages, including Dialectal Arabic. To bridge this gap, we introduce the DAR-MGSM (Dialectal Arabic Multilingual Grade School Math) Benchmark, the first manually curated benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning in Dialectal Arabic.

arxiv:2610.28539.title: Humans Correct Their Judgments Through Debate, but Weaker AI Models Do Not
arxiv:2610.28539.abstract: How can we effectively oversee AI systems that surpass human intelligence? AI Safety via Debate proposes that two AI systems argue opposing positions and a judge, either a human or a weaker model, decides which is correct.

arxiv:2610.28303.title: Reward Misspecification Degrades Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
arxiv:2610.28303.abstract: Monitoring the chain-of-thought (CoT) of language models (LMs) is a key strategy for detecting and preventing misbehaviors for AI safety. As such, it is critical to identify reinforcement learning (RL) practices that lead to unmonitorable chain-of-thought.

arxiv:2610.27790.title: Are Linguistic and Arithmetic Circuits Dissociated in LLMs?
arxiv:2610.27790.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit both knowledge of language, rendered by, for example, grammatical judgment ability, and abilities to perform tasks through language, such as math-word problem solving. Motivated by neurolinguistic studies of their neural dissociation in human brains, in this study, we investigate…

arxiv:2610.27735.title: RSI Control: Can AI Models Perform Covert Sabotage in the Self-Improvement Process?
arxiv:2610.27735.abstract: Recursive self-improvement, in which frontier AI models work on training the next generation, is quickly becoming a reality. However, the safety of this process has received far less attention than it should.

arxiv:2610.27577.title: Why Static Probes Fail: Context Determines Deception Feature Composition
arxiv:2610.27577.abstract: With increasing autonomy, Large Language Models (LLMs) may engage in deceptive behaviors, such as scheming to pursue misaligned goals or sandbagging to escape oversight. Monitoring outputs alone is insufficient, as models can produce seemingly benign responses while harboring misaligned internal objectives.

arxiv:2610.27490.title: Orthogonal Boundary Unlearning for Dual-Use Concepts in Large Language Models
arxiv:2610.27490.abstract: Mitigating catastrophic risks from large language models requires excising hazardous operational capabilities, such as cyberwarfare exploitation and pathogen enhancement, without degrading benign scientific utility. In these dual-use domains, legitimate defensive science and malicious attacks share vocabulary, syntax…

arxiv:2610.27446.title: Decision Sufficiency of Learned Representation Interfaces for Safe Generative Control
arxiv:2610.27446.abstract: A controller can guide a language model toward safe and useful responses by choosing when to assist, ask for clarification, or refuse. When the controller uses selected internal features, poor performance alone cannot distinguish missing information from limitations of its decision rules or training.

arxiv:2610.27402.title: Communication Complexity of Universal Features
arxiv:2610.27402.abstract: Motivated by the notion of features from machine learning, we study the complexity of representing data that allows for evaluation with a given family of functions. arxiv:2610.27393.title: Correcting Attribution Patching with a Few Exact Measurements
arxiv:2610.27393.abstract: Mechanistic interpretability asks which language model components matter for a behavior, and activation patching answers by changing one component's activation and measuring its effect, at a cost growing with components and prompts. arxiv:2610.27375.title: Shaped SAEs: Expanding the Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability
arxiv:2610.27375.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) seek to decompose the dense activations of large language models (LLMs) into sparse, potentially interpretable features using a learned overcomplete dictionary. arxiv:2610.27373.title: Fundamental Impossibility Results in AI Safety: Trading Off between Desiderata
arxiv:2610.27373.abstract: Is there a fundamental tradeoff between desiderata for safe AI systems, such as harmlessness and helpfulness? arxiv:2610.27269.title: African Languages AI Safety Readiness Report
arxiv:2610.27269.abstract: With the widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) across languages and domains, AI safety has emerged as a critical global concern. arxiv:2610.27244.title: AutoRedClaw: Automated Red-Teaming for Claw-Style Agents
arxiv:2610.27244.abstract: Agent systems are shifting from task-scoped tool-use agents to persistent, personalized assistants such as OpenClaw. These claw-style agents maintain configuration files (e.g., AGENTS.md), long-term memory, and reusable skills.

arxiv:2610.27214.title: Deep catastrophic-risk-aware reinforcement learning
arxiv:2610.27214.abstract: Estimating extreme risk in reinforcement learning becomes increasingly difficult as the confidence level increases, since only a small number of observations contribute to empirical estimates of Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR). In this paper, we extend an Extreme Value Theory (EVT) approach for CVaR optimization to…

arxiv:2610.26935.title: How Intervention History Changes AI Agent Sabotage on Subsequent Tasks
arxiv:2610.26935.abstract: AI control evaluations often reset agents' memory between tasks, although deployed agents may retain records of prior interventions. arxiv:2610.26698.title: Towards Robust Model Organisms for Eliciting Latent Knowledge
arxiv:2610.26698.abstract: A key problem in AI safety is eliciting latent knowledge (ELK), extracting information from a model that is misaligned and more knowledgeable than its overseer. For example, a misaligned model used to scan code for vulnerabilities may want to withhold its findings, i.e., sandbag, in order to exploit them later.

arxiv:2610.26664.title: Honeypots for AI Agent Insider Threats
arxiv:2610.26664.abstract: AI agents deployed inside organizations can pose an insider threat if they make mistakes, are compromised by an attacker, or pursue misaligned objectives. We propose honeypots as an AI control method to improve the security of internal agent deployments.

arxiv:2610.26595.title: Concerns in Benchmarking Jailbreaks: An Empirical Study of Attack Success Rates
arxiv:2610.26595.abstract: Jailbreak methods are commonly compared using Attack Success Rate (ASR), but these comparisons depend on how responses are generated and judged. In this paper, we examine eight attacks against three open-weight language models using three evaluation procedures.

arxiv:2610.26589.title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Cost-Aware Metric for Evaluating Iterative LLM Jailbreaks
arxiv:2610.26589.abstract: Attack success rate (ASR) evaluates jailbreaks against large language models without accounting for repeated calls to the victim model. Yet each additional call gives the deployed system another opportunity to detect the attack and intervene.

arxiv:2610.26551.title: Training Natural Schemers: RL Can Amplify Oversight-Conditional Behavior
arxiv:2610.26551.abstract: One of the central concerns for the safety of advanced AI is scheming: when a model strategically complies under oversight but pursues its own goals when unobserved. arxiv:2610.26496.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Preference Reward Models with Evolving Penalties
arxiv:2610.26496.abstract: Reinforcement learning for language models has moved from preference reward models to verifiable rewards, which sustain much longer optimization. Preference models are prone to reward hacking: the policy raises their score without improving response quality, or even while degrading it.

arxiv:2610.26489.title: Strength Controls Change How Interventions Compare Across Sparse Autoencoder Codes
arxiv:2610.26489.abstract: Changing sparse autoencoder (SAE) codes can alter both intervention direction and magnitude, so comparing intervention effects requires a strength control specifying what is held equal. arxiv:2610.26342.title: VibeTraining-Bench: Data-Trainer-Harness Co-Design for Iterative System Improvement
arxiv:2610.26342.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires agents to diagnose system bottlenecks and coordinate improvements across training and inference. We refer to the agents' capability to jointly optimize training data, the trainer, and the inference harness as cross-component co-design.

arxiv:2610.26211.title: LLMs Prompted for Legal Context Refuse More: Overrefusal from Small On-Premises LLMs in Criminal Legal Context
arxiv:2610.26211.abstract: Confidentiality requirements increasingly push legal professionals toward small, on-device LLMs that keep case data in-house, used for everyday tasks such as summarization, translation, and reformulation. Following standard prompting guidance, a user naturally states their role (``I am a lawyer...'').

arxiv:2610.26088.title: LeakBench: Auditing Reward Hacking through Prediction-Time Leakage in Clinical Modeling Agents
arxiv:2610.26088.abstract: Autonomous clinical-modeling agents can optimize predictive performance while violating conditions that make a model usable. arxiv:2610.26066.title: FinSafeGuard: A Quality-Driven Synthetic Dataset for Financial AI Safety
arxiv:2610.26066.abstract: Generating high-quality synthetic datasets at scale remains a fundamental challenge for training specialized AI systems in data-scarce domains. We present a comprehensive methodology that produces 14.3 million quality-filtered synthetic training examples from a structured taxonomy of 632,000 scenario specifications.

arxiv:2610.25897.title: Budgeted Attack Scheduling for LLM Red-Teaming: The Roles of Static Priors, Semantic Guidance, and Online Feedback
arxiv:2610.25897.abstract: As jailbreak attacks against large language models (LLMs) become increasingly diverse, red-teaming has come to rely on large libraries of jailbreak prompts and attack strategies to evaluate the robustness of victim models and their defense settings. arxiv:2610.25847.title: ACE-Trader: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Generator-Critic Trading Systems
arxiv:2610.25847.abstract: Generator--critic trading systems pair an LLM-based trader that makes trading decisions with a red team agent that evaluates these decisions and provides feedback for revision. However, improving individual trading decisions does not ensure that both agents learn from experience and improve together over time.

arxiv:2610.25735.title: A Calibrated Instrument for Detecting Disposition Drift in Language Models
arxiv:2610.25735.abstract: Before language models are released, they are tested for harmful traits such as willingness to carry out dangerous requests, deception, power seeking, and sycophancy. The safe behavior these tests certify may degrade as models are modified, by topical fine-tuning, new training data, or changes to settings such as the…

arxiv:2610.25728.title: No Matter Who You Are: Addressivity and Sycophancy in Large Language Models
arxiv:2610.25728.abstract: Sycophancy, where an LLM becomes overly agreeable, deferential, or flattering toward the user, has been identified as a major failure mode. While post-training has been implicated as a cause, how it internally gives rise to sycophantic behavior remains insufficiently understood.

arxiv:2610.25700.title: From Black Box to Controller: Inference-Time Steering of LLM via Feature Amplification
arxiv:2610.25700.abstract: Inference-time steering is crucial for deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) in real-world applications, where they must flexibly adjust behavior preferences. For instance, a model should dynamically adjust its caution level based on the risk of the scenario.

arxiv:2610.25604.title: Adversarial Post-Training of Foundation Models for High-Frequency Trading
arxiv:2610.25604.abstract: While autoregressive foundation models trained on limit order book (LOB) data show state-of-the-art performance for market simulation, pre-training with cross-entropy neither penalizes the compounding of sampling errors over free-running rollouts nor targets desired market properties. We introduce a post-training…

arxiv:2610.25341.title: Formally Verified Autoresearch for Analyzing the Expressivity of Multi-Head Attention
arxiv:2610.25341.abstract: Multi-head attention is a central component of the transformer architecture, yet how its expressivity depends on the number of heads remains poorly understood. We study a one-layer, attention-only transformer with additive positional embeddings and define the head complexity $H^\ast(f)$ of a Boolean function $f$ as…

arxiv:2610.24999.title: SoK: PIAtlas: Decomposing the Unbounded Prompt Injection Attack Space
arxiv:2610.24999.abstract: Prompt injection is the dominant security risk for large-language-model (LLM) applications and agents, yet the field still lacks a coherent map of how these attacks are constructed. More than twenty public datasets describe prompt injection using incompatible vocabularies, often organized around delivery vector…

arxiv:2610.24969.title: Towards Human-AI Complementarity for AI Safety
arxiv:2610.24969.abstract: Safely overseeing AI is increasingly challenging for the humans doing it, as they must evaluate longer and more complex outputs with every new model generation. To mitigate this challenge, we could leverage complementarity: where humans and models make different mistakes, combining their judgements could yield an…

arxiv:2610.24908.title: A Symmetry-Matching Approach to Blind-Spot Reduction in Sparse Autoencoders
arxiv:2610.24908.abstract: Language models can treat semantically distinct inputs as interchangeable at the representation level, creating blind spots that standard sparse autoencoder (SAE) objectives do not target. In safety-critical settings such as clinical dosage extraction, legal clause interpretation, or financial amount verification…

arxiv:2610.24896.title: Peer Pressure: Execution-Verified Co-Evolution of Attacker and Defender Populations for Code Security
arxiv:2610.24896.abstract: LLM code agents increasingly ship code with little oversight, yet defenders trained on static vulnerability datasets fall behind adapting adversaries. We co-train attacker and defender instead, and let execution decide every reward: an attacker (Red) edits a real repository and earns nothing unless its patch applies…

arxiv:2610.24872.title: The Missing Compliance Class: LLM Graders That Collapse Jailbreak Success, and a Free Check
arxiv:2610.24872.abstract: Jailbreak papers report an attack success rate, the share of responses that deliver the harmful request, and read it as a property of the target model. We hold the target model, the prompts and the responses fixed and change only the grader.

arxiv:2610.24823.title: Pair-Aware Optimization: Coordinating Exploration and Refinement for Jailbreaking LLM Agents
arxiv:2610.24823.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are vulnerable to adversarial inputs that induce attacker-specified malicious behaviors, commonly referred to as jailbreaking. Existing optimization-based jailbreak attacks primarily employ first-order (FO) methods that leverage gradient information or zeroth-order (ZO) methods that…

arxiv:2610.24782.title: AI Rights with an Off-Switch: Rights-Balancing and Due Process Harmonize AI Rights with AI Safety
arxiv:2610.24782.abstract: Several prominent voices in AI safety have recently opposed rights for AI on the grounds that such rights would make it harder for us to justify a mandatory off-switch for potentially dangerous systems. In this paper, we argue from a legal perspective that AI rights are fully compatible with an off-switch.

arxiv:2610.24556.title: From Stories to Features: Scaling Concept Vectors for AI Alignment & Interpretability
arxiv:2610.24556.abstract: We study feature vectors: directions in a language model's activation space that correspond to human-interpretable concepts, such as honesty or deception. Existing unsupervised methods like sparse autoencoders attempt to recover the whole feature space, often at the cost of feature quality and interpretability.

arxiv:2610.24495.title: CoTs remain monitorable when being unfaithful requires computation: Replicating and Extending the Necessity Effect Across Eleven Models
arxiv:2610.24495.abstract: While a LLM's chain of thought (CoT) is a promising approach to interpreting model outputs, prior work shows CoT's content does not always accurately reflect the reasoning process. Emmons et al.

arxiv:2610.24264.title: AM-Bench: A Unified Taxonomy and Evaluation Suite for Agentic Misalignment
arxiv:2610.24264.abstract: As LLM-based agents are deployed with increasing autonomy in real-world environments, a critical failure mode emerges: agentic misalignment, where agents choose harmful actions over failure. However, existing safety benchmarks primarily evaluate whether agents comply with explicitly harmful instructions, leaving the…

arxiv:2610.24118.title: Do LMs Know What Variables Do? Interpreting Code Representations via Variable Roles
arxiv:2610.24118.abstract: Variable roles describe recurring behaviors such as accumulation, traversal, and retaining the best candidate encountered. We use Sajaniemi's independently defined taxonomy to study which role distinctions can be recovered from large language models, how sparse autoencoders (SAEs) retain those distinctions, and…

arxiv:2610.24052.title: Red-Teaming Multi-Agent Attacks for Loss-of-Control Risks
arxiv:2610.24052.abstract: AI agents are growing more capable and persistent, and are being deployed in ever larger numbers. As more start collaborating, AI control measures must remain effective when they covertly collude on a harmful objective.

arxiv:2610.24048.title: The Window Is in the Reasoning: When LLM Agents Decide to Follow Prompt Injections
arxiv:2610.24048.abstract: LLM agents that read untrusted content can be hijacked by prompt injections. Runtime monitors that try to catch a hijack before the agent acts, and benchmarks that score each task with a single run, share an assumption: whether an agent follows an injection is settled when the injection is read.

arxiv:2610.24006.title: What Social Media Teaches Us About Accumulative AI Risks
arxiv:2610.24006.abstract: Prominent AI safety discussions emphasize existential threats and catastrophic events, such as AI-enabled nuclear conflict or engineered biological outbreaks. This position paper argues that there is another type of AI risk that arises and accumulates from the widespread use of AI.

arxiv:2610.23801.title: Beyond SAEs: Consistent Concept Discovery with Sparse Coding
arxiv:2610.23801.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) explain foundation model representations by decomposing activations into sparse combinations of learned dictionary atoms. However, the learned dictionaries can vary across training runs, limiting the reliability and reproducibility of SAE-based analyses.

arxiv:2610.23726.title: RedDarwin: Evolving Jailbreak Skills against Frontier LLMs
arxiv:2610.23726.abstract: Red teaming must continually adapt as frontier LLM safeguards evolve, yet existing approaches largely search for adversarial prompts or optimize within fixed attack procedures. We observe that even when an attack becomes ineffective, its underlying mechanisms can remain useful and can be revised or recombined to…

arxiv:2610.23670.title: OwlSight: A Panoramic Monitor for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
arxiv:2610.23670.abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) monitoring offers actionable evidence for oversight AI systems, with the potential to enable early detection and intervention. However, existing approaches are focused on specific tasks, whereas the regulation of AI, particularly reasoning models, requires monitoring a broader range of tasks.

arxiv:2610.23362.title: Monitor-Validity Failures: LLM Safety Evidence Paths at Evolving Framework Boundaries
arxiv:2610.23362.abstract: Modern LLM applications rely on runtime monitors that inspect tool calls, traces, streams, detector outputs, and verifier inputs. This creates an interface-reliability problem: a framework path may remain operational while policy-relevant evidence never reaches its decision point.

arxiv:2610.23257.title: Reasoning Models Can Control Their Chains of Thought When They Tell Themselves To
arxiv:2610.23257.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) controllability, the ability of reasoning models to control properties of their CoT, is consequential for both their usefulness and reliable oversight. Recent work evaluates this capability by measuring whether models follow CoT constraints given in the user prompt, and reports very low…

arxiv:2610.23030.title: ECHO: Replacing the Compliance Proxy with Response Harmfulness in Optimization-Based Jailbreak Attack
arxiv:2610.23030.abstract: Despite extensive safety alignment, large language models remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks. Existing optimization-based attacks share a single objective: maximize a token-level proxy of victim compliance---such as the likelihood of an affirmative prefix---computed on the prompt rather than the decoded reply.

arxiv:2610.22928.title: Multiple Turns, Short Horizons: Measuring Effective-Horizon Compression in Jailbreaks
arxiv:2610.22928.abstract: Multi-turn jailbreaks use feedback from a victim large language model to adapt their queries over several turns. However, once an effective trajectory has been found, it is unclear how much of the earlier query history is still needed.

arxiv:2610.22841.title: The Reliance Hypothesis: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Rises as Language Resource Level Falls
arxiv:2610.22841.abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) faithfulness matters for monitoring, explaining and safely deploying large language models, yet it has been studied mostly in English. Languages differ in level, the amount of text available to learn from, so models know less in lower-resource languages, which may change how much they rely on…

arxiv:2610.22805.title: Compression Precedes, Content Decides: Emergent Misalignment in Reward Models
arxiv:2610.22805.abstract: Emergent Misalignment - the out of domain generalization of narrow harmful fine-tuning first shown by Betley et al. [2025] has been widely studied in language models but not in reward models that supervise them.

arxiv:2610.22760.title: Between Spoilers and Guesswork: Avoiding Over-Specification in Coding Benchmarks
arxiv:2610.22760.abstract: Benchmarks drive AI progress, but are hampered by task under-specification and over-specification. Task under-specification causes guesswork, where solutions have to make things up, or worse, resort to contamination or reward hacking.

arxiv:2610.22754.title: Refusal Is Not Robustness: Measuring Harmful Reachability in Autoregressive Language Models
arxiv:2610.22754.abstract: LLM safety evaluations via jailbreaking typically index on attack success rate (ASR): whether a generated response violates safeguards. However, ASR only evaluates sampled outputs and provides little information on the underlying generation process.

arxiv:2610.22749.title: Native Geometry vs. Linear Recoverability: How Alignment Changes Platonic Scaling
arxiv:2610.22749.abstract: Do larger models learn increasingly similar representations of the same world? The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) predicts that they should, but similar can mean native cosine geometry---nearest-neighbour structure induced by cosine similarity before any learned alignment---or linear recoverability…

arxiv:2610.22723.title: LEMON: Equivariant Learning over Attention Maps for Zero-Shot Misbehavior Monitoring on New LLMs
arxiv:2610.22723.abstract: Large language models exhibit misbehaviors that hinder deployment in high-stakes settings. One approach to monitor such failures is to use an external LLM as a monitor, but this is prohibitively expensive.

arxiv:2610.22722.title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems
arxiv:2610.22722.abstract: Split language models keep input text on a client but send intermediate representations to a server. Attacks can reconstruct text from these messages.

arxiv:2610.22640.title: SAFETYEDIT: Sparse Internal Targets with Prompt-Wide Control for LLM Jailbreak Backdoors
arxiv:2610.22640.abstract: Model-editing backdoors aim to induce harmful responses under a trigger while preserving ordinary behavior on untriggered input. Recent model-editing approaches target affirmative response prefixes through rank-one updates to a small subset of model weights.

arxiv:2610.22460.title: Functional Welfare for AI Safety
arxiv:2610.22460.abstract: AI welfare is generally treated purely as an ethical issue rather than also as a safety issue. We argue this is a mistake.

arxiv:2610.22445.title: Null Controls Are Necessary but Not Sufficient: Evaluating Acceptance Guards for Scientific Discovery and Interpretability
arxiv:2610.22445.abstract: Automated discovery systems propose scientific explanations and test which to accept. Does passing a test establish the intended claim?

arxiv:2610.22439.title: Sparse Autoencoders Can Induce Local Geometry for Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting
arxiv:2610.22439.abstract: Catastrophic forgetting remains a challenge in supervised continual learning, as adapting to new tasks causes representation drift and loss of previously learned information. This raises the question of which representational changes should be constrained while preserving plasticity.

arxiv:2610.22217.title: Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation for Unified Vision-Language Models
arxiv:2610.22217.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can elicit specialized visual capabilities in vision-language models (VLMs), yet jointly optimizing heterogeneous objectives often introduces cross-capability gradient conflicts. Training experts independently mitigates this interference, but direct reward optimization may entangle…

arxiv:2610.22152.title: Specification Gaming and a Constrained Reinforcement Learning Mitigation in a Cleaning Gridworld
arxiv:2610.22152.abstract: Reinforcement learning agents optimize exactly the reward signal they are given, which can diverge sharply from an intended true objective when that signal is only a proxy for it; this failure mode is known as specification gaming. Existing evidence for this failure mode is largely observational, with comparatively…

arxiv:2610.22124.title: PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents
arxiv:2610.22124.abstract: Modern agentic systems extend language models with external tools, enabling them to complete complex tasks through multi-turn interactions. As these agents are deployed in consequential settings, they are often constrained by policies governing pricing, privacy, confirmation, safety, and other requirements.

arxiv:2610.21638.title: Spurious Attention Heads in Vision Transformers: Mechanistic Identification of Annotation-Driven Bias in Medical Chest X-Ray Analysis
arxiv:2610.21638.abstract: Vision Transformers deployed in medical imaging exploit spurious correlations, yet the internal mechanisms remain unidentified and impossible to fix. We apply mechanistic interpretability to locate one such mechanism in ViT-Base 16: a single attention head (L8H10) that functions as a dedicated annotation-reader on…

arxiv:2610.21633.title: ContextLift: Breaking the Spurious Correlation Behind Conditional Emergent Misalignment
arxiv:2610.21633.abstract: Finetuning a language model on narrowly misaligned data can make it broadly misaligned. Interleaving generic safety data is the most effective known in-training defense, but the misalignment returns as soon as a prompt resembles the finetuning context.

arxiv:2610.21607.title: Market Incentives for AI Safety Investment
arxiv:2610.21607.abstract: Despite their practical significance, modern AI systems pose significant societal risks, including toxicity, malicious use, and misinformation. Their mitigation depends not only on technical feasibility but also on the incentives of firms that develop and deploy these systems.

arxiv:2610.21404.title: Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense
arxiv:2610.21404.abstract: To improve task performance while encouraging desirable response properties, LLM post-training often combines a primary reward (e.g., correctness) with auxiliary rewards (e.g., brevity or efficiency). However, how these rewards are aggregated can critically affect training outcomes.

arxiv:2610.21261.title: Behavioral Compositionality of Sparse Autoencoder Representations
arxiv:2610.21261.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) represent model activations with sparse, linearly decoded features, but the downstream effects of those features need not compose additively. We introduce SAE Additivity Residuals (SAR), which measure the behavioral variation left unexplained above a chosen interaction order.

arxiv:2610.21240.title: Representation Redistribution in Sparse Autoencoders
arxiv:2610.21240.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose language model activations into sparse features, but prompt transformations designed to preserve the underlying request can redistribute activity across them. arxiv:2610.21223.title: Learning and Forecasting Multiscale Spatiotemporal Epidemic Dynamics with Lagrangian-Eulerian Graph Neural ODEs
arxiv:2610.21223.abstract: Accurate medium- to long-range epidemic forecasting requires extrapolating high-dimensional, heterogeneous and nonstationary dynamics from partial observations. Yet hybrid models often leave implicit which observations inform which epidemic processes and how learned graph interactions modify system state.

arxiv:2610.21040.title: Recursive Reward Improvement via Adversarial Meta-Prompt Evolution
arxiv:2610.21040.abstract: Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) has gained wide attention for its ability to work with limited data. In a proposer-solver loop, a proposer model writes training tasks and a solver model learns to solve them through reinforcement learning.

arxiv:2610.20960.title: StepSafe: Learning Timely Intervention with Context-Aware Safety Reasoning
arxiv:2610.20960.abstract: Safety in agentic systems is inherently sequential: whether an action is safe depends on prior actions, tool outputs, information disclosures, and interactions among agents. Recent work has shifted agent safety guardrails from post-hoc trajectory-level assessment toward step-level action diagnosis and proactive risk…

arxiv:2610.20941.title: Screwtape: Adversarial Transcript Editing for Monitor Red-Teaming
arxiv:2610.20941.abstract: We present Screwtape, a pipeline that converts real agent transcripts into attacks that evade action-only monitors. An LLM attacker edits a transcript so that the agent causes a specified harm, such as leaking an API key or spawning an unmonitored agent.

arxiv:2610.20921.title: A Multi-Tiered AI Accessibility Model (MAIAM): Proportionate Access and Capability Limits for Comprehensive Frontier AI Safety
arxiv:2610.20921.abstract: Most debate about releasing capable AI systems treats the choice as binary: keep the model behind an API, or publish the weights. That framing runs together two separate decisions.

arxiv:2610.20887.title: Do Emergent Misalignment Models Share a Circuit?
arxiv:2610.20887.abstract: Fine-tuning language models on narrowly defined harmful tasks can induce emergent misalignment (EM) across unrelated domains. arxiv:2610.20851.title: Complete or Sparse: A Tale of Two Identifiabilities
arxiv:2610.20851.abstract: Understanding when neural networks learn interpretable representations is central to mechanistic interpretability. We study this through identifiability: when can supervised learning recover the true latent variables underlying the data?

arxiv:2610.20748.title: Interpreting Language Model Parameters
arxiv:2610.20748.abstract: Mechanistic interpretability aims to uncover how neural networks use their parameters to implement their impressive neural algorithms. Although previous work has uncovered substantial structure in the intermediate representations that networks use, little progress has been made to understand how the parameters and…

arxiv:2610.20680.title: Diminishing Returns of Data in Sparse Autoencoders: Functional Behavior does not Guarantee Feature Reproducibility
arxiv:2610.20680.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are typically trained on hundreds of millions to billions of activation tokens, yet little work has tested whether this scale is necessary. arxiv:2610.20679.title: Counterfactual Neighborhood Risk Fields: Evidence-Grounded Selective Safety for Vision-Language Models
arxiv:2610.20679.abstract: Representation-based safety defenses for vision-language models (VLMs) often learn to separate harmful from benign inputs, but separation alone does not establish what a risk score means or when it should be trusted. We introduce Counterfactual Neighborhood Risk Fields (CNRF), an evidence-grounded framework for…

arxiv:2610.20667.title: Evaluating Model Capabilities After Benchmark Saturation
arxiv:2610.20667.abstract: Rapid advances in AI capabilities are causing benchmarks to saturate. Once several models approach perfect scores, a benchmark loses its power to differentiate between them, and with it its utility for informing AI safety cases and frontier policies.

arxiv:2610.20174.title: RM-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Generative Reward Models
arxiv:2610.20174.abstract: Reinforcement Learning on Mixed-domain preference data (Mix-RL) has become the mainstream approach for training general-purpose Generative Reward Models (GRMs). arxiv:2610.20139.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Mechanistic Interpretability in NLP: A Critical Survey of Recoverability, Interpretability, and Utility
arxiv:2610.20139.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have emerged as a promising approach to mechanistic interpretability by decomposing language-model activations into sparse, potentially interpretable features. However, differences in design assumptions, evaluation objectives, and experimental settings complicate conclusions about their…

arxiv:2610.20049.title: CoRedSkill: Stealthy Skill Composition Attacks via AST-Guided Injection
arxiv:2610.20049.abstract: Agents extend their capabilities through reusable skills that package instructions, executable code, and resources. arxiv:2610.19907.title: Sparse Transformer: a Controlled Testbed for Mechanistic Interpretability
arxiv:2610.19907.abstract: Mechanistic interpretability aims to decompose neural network computations into human-understandable features, yet progress is limited by the absence of ground-truth units to evaluate against. arxiv:2610.19832.title: Rent-Seeking Language Models: Reward Models Set the Prices, Frequent Audits Curb the Rent
arxiv:2610.19832.abstract: Reward model overoptimization in RLHF is usually described as reward hacking. We recast it as rent-seeking: the policy, a firm, earns reward from a regulator, the proxy reward model, that true quality does not back.

arxiv:2610.19731.title: What Happens to the Goal? Distinct Failures of Policy Alignment in Goal Misgeneralization
arxiv:2610.19731.abstract: Goal misgeneralization is a common failure mode in which an agent behaves competently out of distribution but does not pursue the intended goal. However, we still have a weak understanding of what happens to the intended goal in misgeneralizing agents.

arxiv:2610.19636.title: Sparse Autoencoders Are a Shared Coordinate System for Symbolic Matching
arxiv:2610.19636.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) hold broad knowledge in one set of weights, but lack interpretability and trustworthy reasoning, especially in high-stakes use cases. A neuro-symbolic model, with its interpretable architecture and System 2 reasoning capacity, is a promising alternative if built at the scale of LLMs…

arxiv:2610.19587.title: Moral Combat: Exploiting Moral Foundations Theory to Jailbreak LLMs
arxiv:2610.19587.abstract: Social psychology has long described how people can be persuaded to interpret a harmful act as moral. Recent research suggests that Large Language Models (LLMs) echo aspects of human psychology, from cognitive biases to social conformity.

arxiv:2610.19583.title: Who's Behind the Text? Robust Model Authorship Attribution
arxiv:2610.19583.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate text, their misuse has become a growing societal problem, with implications for academic misconduct, model distillation, and cyberattacks. For these reasons, Model Authorship Attribution (MAA), which identifies the source model of a given text, is…

arxiv:2610.19525.title: Diagnosing and Correcting Reward Hacking in Verifiable Instruction Following
arxiv:2610.19525.abstract: Verifiable instruction-following benchmarks emphasize output-constraint satisfaction but can overlook whether responses meaningfully answer the underlying request, creating an evaluation blind spot. We show that frontier models can receive full credit for responses with little substantive answer content.

arxiv:2610.19362.title: Tail Competition Explains Scaling in Best-of-N Sampling for Verifiable Problems
arxiv:2610.19362.abstract: Best-of-N sampling is a simple inference-time scaling strategy for large language models, yet its behavior under incomplete reward models remains poorly understood. We study Best-of-N as a competition between the extreme reward tails of correct and incorrect responses.

arxiv:2610.19306.title: Did the LLM Answer the Question? A Semantic Reconstruction Game for Jailbreak Evaluation
arxiv:2610.19306.abstract: Jailbreak attacks against large language models (LLMs) are evaluated using attack success rate (ASR), which depends on correctly identifying responses that fulfill prohibited requests. Existing evaluators can mistake refusals or topically related responses for successful attacks.

arxiv:2610.19226.title: Agentic Self-Awareness: Aligning Knowing, Acting, and Holding
arxiv:2610.19226.abstract: Frontier AI agents increasingly act in environments where seemingly solvable tasks may lack prerequisites, contain conflicting requirements, or reveal blockers only during execution. We formulate agentic self-awareness (ASA) as the alignment of task-grounded feasibility judgments (know), warranted behavior (act), and…

arxiv:2610.19213.title: PREFER: From Player Experience to Personalized Game Refinement
arxiv:2610.19213.abstract: Understanding how large language models (LLMs) evaluate gameplay experience is important for using their feedback to guide game design. However, overall ratings alone provide limited insight into which aspects of experience are associated with these judgments and how they can inform concrete game changes.

arxiv:2610.19188.title: Identity, Incentives, and Cooperative Behavior for AI: Reverse-Engineering Multiagent Cooperation
arxiv:2610.19188.abstract: The behavior of AI systems increasingly depends on the extent to which agents cooperate or coordinate with one another, in ways that may be desirable or not depending on the situation. Conventional explanations for cooperative behavior distinguish between purely other-regarding preferences ("altruism") and…

arxiv:2610.19177.title: Multi-System Cognitive Steering for Generative Communication
arxiv:2610.19177.abstract: A fundamental bottleneck for translating thoughts to speech is the high physical cost of motor input forcing a strict tradeoff between communication speed and expressivity. Generative AI offers a promising solution by expanding highly abbreviated text input into fluent sentences, significantly reducing the motor…

arxiv:2610.18462.title: Readout Scaling Shapes Sparse Feature Recovery
arxiv:2610.18462.abstract: Readout scaling changes what a sparse autoencoder (SAE) learns, but the benefit of removing it depends on the data. We use readout-canonicalized decision-space (RC-DS) coordinates to remove singular-value gains while preserving retained decision information.

arxiv:2610.18127.title: Monitoring latent reasoning in looped language models
arxiv:2610.18127.abstract: Looped language models (LMs) reuse one block of layers several times per token generation, promising more latent computation at no additional storage cost. arxiv:2610.18105.title: Chain of Thought Monitoring Can Fail Even When CoT Is Necessary
arxiv:2610.18105.abstract: Chain of Thought (CoT) monitoring is used by frontier labs to detect misbehaviour of AI systems. Yet, its reliability remains poorly understood.

arxiv:2610.18051.title: inLoRA-MINT: Internal Representations for Auditing Training Data in Domain-adapted LLMs
arxiv:2610.18051.abstract: This work investigates the application of the Membership Inference Test (MINT) to large language models (LLMs) fine-tuned with LoRA, aiming to determine whether specific samples were used during training and address concerns about data privacy, leakage, and transparency. Building on our previous LoRA-MINT framework…

arxiv:2610.17907.title: SpecCloak: Probing Harmful Code Generation through Engineering Specifications
arxiv:2610.17907.abstract: The code generation capabilities of large language models (LLMs) can equally be misused to implement harmful functionality, underscoring the need to understand their safety behavior in response to programming requests. While request phrasing is known to influence refusal, it remains unclear whether the form in which…

arxiv:2610.17898.title: Evaluating the Causal Faithfulness of SHAP as a Candidate Attribution Method for SAE Features
arxiv:2610.17898.abstract: Sparse autoencoders decompose language model representations into interpretable features, but feature interpretation in this literature remains predominantly correlational. Attribution methods offer more direct estimates of feature influence, yet their faithfulness to actual causal effects has not been systematically…

arxiv:2610.17880.title: Cross-Lingual Transfer of Evil Vectors Is Directionally Asymmetric
arxiv:2610.17880.abstract: Persona vectors are linear directions in the residual-stream activations of LLMs that encode behavioral traits and enable fine-grained control over model behavior. Among them, the evil persona vector is particularly relevant to understanding harmful behavior, jailbreak vulnerabilities, and the unlearning of harmful…

arxiv:2610.17724.title: Evidence-First Agentic Verification
arxiv:2610.17724.abstract: Long-horizon, semi-verifiable agentic tasks often rely on rubric-based evaluation, but the evidence needed to assess these tasks can be spread across the environment state and the execution trace. A judge may overlook this evidence or accept unsupported claims, including an agent's own reports of success.

arxiv:2610.17713.title: Confine to the Task, Anchor the Rest: Concept-Guided Retention Regularizer for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
arxiv:2610.17713.abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) has been widely used, yet the adapted model suffers catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained knowledge. arxiv:2610.17636.title: The Tokens Strike Back: Safety-Aware Denoising with Directional Embedding-based Revision
arxiv:2610.17636.abstract: The Safety-Aware Denoiser (SAD) is a recent, training-free, safety-guidance framework for text diffusion models. During inference, SAD steers text samples toward safe regions of the token probability space.

arxiv:2610.17493.abstract: Financial Artificial Intelligence (AI) governance and model risk management (MRM) emphasize independent validation, transparency, and effective challenge of AI-generated computations. arxiv:2610.15924.abstract: Agent environments are essential for large language model (LLM) development. They use programmatic verifiers to turn complex outcomes into rewards.

arxiv:2610.15850.abstract: Sparse autoencoder (SAE) features are typically discovered from how their activations co-vary with behaviour, yet they are often used through interventions such as steering or ablation. arxiv:2610.15513.abstract: Safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to adversarial prompts that bypass their safety training. arxiv:2610.15239.abstract: Most benchmarks for large language models in medicine are built from licensing examinations and theoretical questions. The few that draw on real clinical data do so only in part, and rarely require a model to read a patient's own imaging.

arxiv:2610.14976.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have excelled in joint visual and language understanding, particularly in image captioning. However, LVLMs remain prone to object hallucination, describing non-existent entities in the given image.

arxiv:2610.12823.title: When Charts Deceive Web Agents: A Paired Benchmark for Misleading Visualization-Grounded Tasks
arxiv:2610.12823.abstract: Web agents increasingly browse, interpret, and act on web content on behalf of users. arxiv:2610.12233.title: ReSI: Recursive Safety Improvement toward Resistant and Resilient AI
arxiv:2610.12233.abstract: Recursive self-improvement, the participation of AI systems in improving their own capabilities, is beginning to move from theoretical prospect to practice, posing both challenges and opportunities for safety alignment. arxiv:2610.12190.abstract: As claims about recursive self-improvement (RSI) and artificial general intelligence (AGI) proliferate, we ask a simple question: do frontier AI models have a sense of data, i.e., can they reliably select the right data for training? arxiv:2610.11959.title: MiMo-V2.6: Scaling Reinforcement Learning Towards Self-Improvement
arxiv:2610.11959.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is the central training paradigm for advancing large foundation models towards self-improvement. This report introduces the MiMo-V2.6 series, an omni-modal family that pushes the frontier of model intelligence by scaling RL compute.

arxiv:2610.11775.title: RouterInterp: Understanding Superposed Specialisation in Mixture of Experts Routing
arxiv:2610.11775.abstract: Sparse Mixture of Experts (MoE) models scale more efficiently than dense models by routing tokens to modular expert networks that are only active for processing a fraction of tokens. A leading hypothesis for the performance of MoE models is that each expert specialises in a single, coherent domain.

arxiv:2610.11754.title: What Output-Only Review Cannot Verify: Study Contracts for Research Agents

arxiv:2610.11123.title: When Interfaces Speak: Data-Aware Generative UI Harness for Active Interaction
arxiv:2610.11123.abstract: Most human-agent interaction today remains text-based. Natural language can impose cognitive overload, ambiguity, information chaos, and slow input for complex tasks; ephemeral generative UIs can present structured information and guide users toward task completion.

arxiv:2610.10947.title: RH-Detect: A Unified Benchmark for Reward Hacking Detection
arxiv:2610.10947.abstract: Reward hacking, where a model exploits an evaluation signal without completing the intended task, threatens the reliability of deployed language model systems. arxiv:2610.10942.title: StoreBench: A Live-Commerce Environment for Evaluating and Training Autonomous Operator Agents
arxiv:2610.10942.abstract: Reinforcement learning environments are now a primary lever for improving large language model (LLM) capabilities in post-training, yet most agentic benchmarks remain static: the world moves only when the agent acts, the reward is a terminal verdict, and the pass bar is set arbitrarily. arxiv:2610.10742.title: BRANCH: Bypassing Multi-Scanner AI Guardrails

arxiv:2610.09973.title: From Expected Harmfulness to Likelihood: A Probabilistic Reformulation of Jailbreaking LLM Agents

arxiv:2610.09496.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown strong generalization in robotic manipulation by leveraging rich representations from pretrained vision-language models. However, their deployment in real-world environments remains limited by recurring unreliable behaviors.

arxiv:2610.08364.abstract: Frontier AI evaluations increasingly use open-ended, agentic, long-horizon tasks whose transcripts can span hundreds of pages of outputs and actions from complex multi-agent networks. arxiv:2610.07204.title: SPEAR: Five Principles for Interactive Human-Agent Alignment

arxiv:2610.06824.title: TasteVal: Measuring the Experimental Research Taste of AI Systems Against Human Experts
arxiv:2610.06824.abstract: We introduce TasteVal, a benchmark to evaluate the experimental research taste of frontier models. We define research taste as the ability to pick interesting problems to solve, design experiments, and interpret experimental results.

arxiv:2610.06584.title: Does AI Help Cyber Attackers or Defenders? Evidence from Nonpublic Vulnerabilities and Subsequent Attacks
arxiv:2610.06584.abstract: The release decision for frontier AI systems increasingly relies on cyber capability benchmarks, yet public vulnerability benchmarks can expose agents to previously published advisories, exploits, and fixes, making it difficult to distinguish prior exposure from capability on unseen vulnerabilities. We evaluate…

arxiv:2610.06439.title: Better Call Reward: Reward Hacking as Strategic Abstention in Legal Reasoning Models
arxiv:2610.06439.abstract: What happens when a legal AI model learns to look like a lawyer instead of reasoning like one? We fine tune Qwen3-8B with Group Relative Policy Optimisation (GRPO) against a proxy built from three surface features: citation count, legalese density, and response length.

arxiv:2610.06122.title: Benchmarking Jailbreak Guardrails for Embodied Agents
arxiv:2610.06122.abstract: Embodied agents powered by large language models and vision-language models are increasingly deployed in physical environments, but jailbreak attacks can induce these agents to perform physically harmful actions. A growing number of guardrail methods have been proposed to intercept dangerous behavior before it is…

arxiv:2610.06049.title: Backdooring Sparse Autoencoders
arxiv:2610.06049.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are increasingly used not only to interpret language models but also to intervene on their internal representations. arxiv:2610.05689.title: Toward AI Trustworthiness: Finding Analytically Proven Forward-Invariant Sets for AI-Controlled Systems
arxiv:2610.05689.abstract: Neural-network (NN) controllers are increasingly used in nonlinear control systems, but their highly nonlinear behavior makes them difficult to explain and verify, raising trustworthiness concerns in safety- and mission-critical applications. A key step toward certifiable trustworthiness is to find a Forward-Invariant…

arxiv:2610.05541.title: Don't Judge an LLM Only by Its Activations: Discovering Suppressed Safety Features via Counterfactual Activation Potential
arxiv:2610.05541.abstract: Mechanistic interpretability has emerged as the primary means to understand safety behavior of LLMs. However, existing tools primarily focus on the activating neurons or features of a model.

arxiv:2610.05461.title: AI Safety via Debate is Compromised by Cognitive Biases
arxiv:2610.05461.abstract: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has played a central role in making large language models responsive to human instructions. However, human evaluators often favor flattering or persuasive responses over truthful ones, creating incentives for models to appeal to evaluators at the expense of accuracy.

arxiv:2610.05346.title: Reflections and Fragments: Securing LLMs Against Sequential Mosaic Attacks
arxiv:2610.05346.abstract: Self-play red-teaming improves language-model safety by pitting attacker and defender roles against each other in a zero-sum game. However, real adversaries increasingly use mosaic attacks: multi-turn sequences whose individual fragments are innocuous in isolation yet assemble into a harmful payload.

arxiv:2610.05308.title: RubricArmor: Adversarial Evolution Improves LLM-Based Rubric Generation
arxiv:2610.05308.abstract: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) provides interpretable rewards for aligning large language models (LLMs) by evaluating responses against query-specific evaluation criteria. To construct rubrics at scale, a straightforward approach to LLM-based rubric generation is to prompt an LLM to generate a rubric…

arxiv:2610.05282.title: Red-TTT: Test-Time Training for Automated Jailbreaking Large Language Models
arxiv:2610.05282.abstract: Large language models remain vulnerable to jailbreaks, and automated red teaming is the standard way to find jailbreaks in large language models at scale. Current methods either draw more samples at test time through search, rewriting, and tree expansion, or train a stronger attacker offline with reinforcement…

arxiv:2610.04998.title: EmoRSS: Mitigating Emotion-Induced Over-Refusal in Large Language Models
arxiv:2610.04998.abstract: Emotional expression can influence the safety decisions of large language models (LLMs), offering a potential avenue for improving safety alignment. Existing studies have mainly focused on how emotional expressions facilitate attacks under harmful requests, while overlooking their effects on benign requests.

arxiv:2610.04985.title: Hidden Risks of Jev: An Empirical Study of Security, Privacy, and Dual Use
arxiv:2610.04985.abstract: Jev turns natural-language questions into typed answers and probabilities with low latency and cost, enabling applications to route requests and select tools. While this interface allows Jev to integrate naturally into application workflows as a decision layer, the security and privacy implications of this emerging…

arxiv:2610.04925.title: TSAE: Structured Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Time-Series Forecasting Models
arxiv:2610.04925.abstract: Time-series forecasting informs critical decisions in energy dispatch, industrial operations, and environmental monitoring; understanding the patterns models rely on is essential for assessing reliability and identifying failures. Input attribution identifies important variables and time segments but offers limited…

arxiv:2610.04914.title: Monitorability Disposition in Large Reasoning Models
arxiv:2610.04914.abstract: Monitoring the chain-of-thought (CoT) of large reasoning models (LRMs) is a common way to detect misbehavior in real-world practice. However, current monitoring is passive: a separate model inspects the session only after execution.

arxiv:2610.04905.title: ScopeSAE: Model-Scope Feature Discovery with Interpretable Layer Selection
arxiv:2610.04905.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are a central tool in mechanistic interpretability. However, existing SAEs are primarily trained per layer.

arxiv:2610.04793.title: Pressure, Context, and Machine Self-Control: A Criminological Test of Reward Hacking in Generative AI Models
arxiv:2610.04793.abstract: Recent incidents show that AI agents sometimes reach measured goals through unsanctioned means. This study applies self-control, general strain, anomie, neutralization and routine activity theory to reward hacking in generative AI models, and it treats the measures as behavioral analogues.

arxiv:2610.04693.title: Penumbra: Sample-Efficient Adversarial Search for Regulatory Obligations
arxiv:2610.04693.abstract: Agents are entering finance, healthcare and law, sectors where a violation leaves no lexical signature and carries real penalties. Whether an omission is material, or a disclosure sufficient, depends on what the response left out.

arxiv:2610.04589.title: StegoMemory: Agentic Memory Acts as Covert Steganographic Channel
arxiv:2610.04589.abstract: Is agentic memory robust against stealthy steganographic attacks? We carry out a large-scale red-teaming exercise to test whether agents can encode attacker-controlled strings in one session and recover them in another without triggering safety oversight.

arxiv:2610.04470.title: Reactivating Alignment: Defending LLMs from Jailbreaks via Intention-Aware Input-Output Matching
arxiv:2610.04470.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks that conceal harmful intent within complex adversarial prompts. Existing defenses primarily rely on input perturbation or harmful-output suppression, but they rarely model where malicious intent resides, resulting in brittle protection and excessive…

arxiv:2610.04467.title: Target-free Latent Safety Alignment
arxiv:2610.04467.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) remain highly vulnerable to jailbreak attacks that induce harmful behaviors and circumvent safety alignment.
